perf.summary: Inner loop recomputes i*j and i*j again for indexing, and the guard multiply per j is redundant; strength-reduce to an additive walk.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop `for (int j=1; (long)i*j<=n; j++) result[i*j] += fi*g[j]` performs, per iteration: one 64-bit multiply for the guard `(long)i*j`, plus an `int` multiply `i*j` for the index. That is two multiplies per inner step over an O(n log n) total iteration count.
perf.proposedChange: Replace with an index that advances by i: `for (int ij = i, j = 1; ij <= n; ij += i, j++) result[ij] += fi * g[j];`. This eliminates both multiplies per iteration (the running `ij` serves as both guard and index) at the cost of one add. Since `i*j <= n <= int range` along the valid path, `ij` stays in int; the original `(long)i*j` guard was only protecting overflow of the boundary test, which `ij += i` with `ij <= n` handles without overflow because n bounds it.
perf.rationale: Removes one 64-bit imul and one 32-bit imul per inner iteration (replaced by a single add), shortening the dependency chain and improving Burst vectorization/throughput on the dominant O(n log n) work.
perf.risk: `ij += i` could overflow int only if it exceeded int.MAX before the `ij <= n` check; since each accepted ij <= n and the next is ij+i <= n+i, choose `n` within `int.MAX - n` headroom (true for any valid n < ~2^30). Guard: if n can approach int.MAX, keep ij as long. Semantics identical otherwise.

perf.summary: Identical strength-reduction: drop the per-iteration multiplies in the inner convolution loop, and hoist f[i] read.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop `for (int j=1; (long)i*j<=n; j++) h[i*j] += f[i]*g[j]` does a 64-bit guard multiply and a 32-bit index multiply per iteration, and re-reads `f[i]` from memory each inner iteration instead of hoisting it to a local.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist `long fi = f[i];` (the function already checks f[i]==0 but then re-reads f[i] inside) and rewrite as `for (int ij = i, j = 1; ij <= n; ij += i, j++) h[ij] += fi * g[j];`. Mirrors the fix in ConvolutionPrefixSum.
perf.rationale: Eliminates two multiplies plus a redundant load per inner iteration over O(n log n) iterations; shorter dependency chain, fewer cache-touch reads of f[i].
perf.risk: Same int-overflow-of-ij caveat as above; safe for n within int headroom. Hoisting f[i] is pure since f is not aliased to h in valid usage (separate buffers) — if caller aliases f and h, behavior could change, but that is already an undefined/unsupported aliasing case.

perf.summary: Two separate zeroing passes over result can be fused / replaced; result[0]=0 then a 1..n zero loop duplicates initialization.
perf.currentCost: `result[0]=0` then `for(i=1;i<=n;i++) result[i]=0` zeroes the whole array in a scalar loop. This is a separate full pass before the accumulation loop.
perf.proposedChange: Zero the buffer as a single contiguous span (e.g. a Unsafe-style memclear / a single loop from 0..n already covers index 0, removing the special-case `result[0]=0` and the `n==0` early return needs only the `result[0]=0` guard kept). At minimum merge: `for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) result[i] = 0;` removing the duplicated result[0] write.
perf.rationale: Removes a redundant store and a branch; a single straight memclear is trivially vectorizable by Burst and avoids the scalar per-element loop. Constant-factor only but free.
perf.risk: Must preserve the `n==0` early-return semantics (after writing result[0]=0). Keep the `if(n<0) return;` guard. No behavioral change for n>=0.

perf.summary: The Sqrt-derived bound u can be off by one due to double rounding, and the two loops recompute n/d divisions that could be partly shared; also fd/gd are simple adjacent differences.
perf.currentCost: `u = (long)Math.Sqrt((double)n)` can round down (or rarely up) for large n where double cannot represent n exactly, producing a u that is 1 too small or too large. While the hyperbola identity is robust to which exact split point is used as long as u*limit2 partitioning is consistent, an off-by-one u changes `limit2 = n/u` and the correction term, which must satisfy u == n/(n/u)-region consistency. Separately each loop does a 64-bit idiv `n/d` per iteration (unavoidable) but the `fd = prefixF[d]-prefixF[d-1]` is a redundant pair of loads when iterating sequentially.
perf.proposedChange: After computing u via Sqrt, correct it deterministically: `while ((u+1)*(u+1) <= n) u++; while (u*u > n) u--;` so u is exactly floor(sqrt(n)) independent of FPU rounding. For the difference terms, carry a running `prev = prefixF[d-1]` across iterations so each step is one load + one subtract instead of two loads.
perf.rationale: The integer-correction makes the result deterministic and portable across PC/mobile FPUs (purity/correctness) at negligible cost (1-2 iterations). Carrying prev halves the prefix-array loads in each O(sqrt n) loop, reducing cache traffic.
perf.risk: (u+1)*(u+1) can overflow for n near long.MAX (~3.0e18 -> u~1.7e9, (u+1)^2 fits in long up to ~9.2e18, so safe for all valid n). The carried-prev rewrite must reset correctly at d=1 using prefixF[0]. Behavior identical for all n where the original Sqrt happened to be exact; for inexact cases the corrected version is the mathematically correct floor(sqrt), which is the intended value.
